episodes.name: episode 3
episodes.material: soprano imitates final run of CS; new figure (foreshadowed in prelude bars 23-24) followed by tenor in canon at fifth; false entry bar 19
episodes.sequence: falling sequence touching bVII, v, III, i

episodes.name: episode 4

episodes.sequence: canonic sequence touching III, i, VI, iv

episodes.name: episode 5

countersubjects.notes: contains three ideas: opening semiquaver run, falling crotchet steps, final semiquaver run; opening run inverted at 9 and 13 because answer and subject differ in first five notes; frequently fragmented between voices

subject.answer: tonal: first five notes treated as non-modulating (dominant f# answered by tonic b), then all intervals of the subject from this lowered pitch, so the answer ends in the tonic
subject.notes: subject modulates to dominant and uses every note of the chromatic scale

claims.claim: Subject uses every note of the chromatic scale
Most of the fugue is in three parts; four parts reserved for climactic passages, about one-fifth of the total length
Answer treats the first five notes as non-modulating; unlike I.18
Episodes contain 'false entries' of the subject (bars 19, 28, 34, 35, 41, 42, 43)
Tenor entry at 44 times its arrival like the false entries but is a complete subject
From bar 53 texture is three-part; four-part resumes at bar 70, five-part before the end
Final section presumed to begin at 69 though it is only a partial entry
